Overview, reorganised

Your request (12 Nov): a well organised Overview with no extra space and no useless text, and without the two page-foot buttons. Your review of the first sample (12 Nov): "looks good, but remove extra useless data". This revision removes the chosen loop's zoom tools, its live/feed/time line and the loop's name, and the name and section from every queue row, so each row is one line. This changes the Overview only. The ten KPI drill-downs stay exactly as they are. The app's sizes stay as they are: 94 px KPI cards, 40 px buttons, 14 px text, the app's pill sizes and the 260 px trend. Lab today: 241 of 243 loops monitored, Stale 165, Never evaluated 76, every other card 0, and no current finding. The busy-plant state in the sample is illustrative.

The reader's path, top to bottom

  1. How is the fleet? The ten cards, with "241 loops monitored" said once above them. The second row ends with the cards that say how far the numbers can be trusted (Not assessable, Stale and Never evaluated), and Stale keeps its amber edge.
  2. What needs me? Loops requiring review: up to six rows in priority order, one line each (priority, tag, state, diagnosis, in band). When there are none, it is one line: "No current findings".
  3. The chosen loop. Named by its tag, with its live values and 8 h trend, beside the rows. The top row is chosen by default. Review → opens Investigation.
  4. What happened lately? Recent events: the three newest episodes. All events → opens the full list.
  5. How is it counted? How to read, top right, opened when needed.

What stays exactly

HeaderEyebrow Find problems, title Overview, no ?, no sentence. 12h / 24h stays top right, is kept in ?window= and is carried by every link. The plant scope comes from the header (site, area, unit) and narrows the cards, the queue and the events.
Ten KPI cardsToday's labels, order and coloured icons; 94 px tall; green edge on Performing acceptably above 0, amber on a problem card above 0. Share and rule on hover. Each card opens its drill-down /cpm?review=<kpi>&window=…. The drill-downs do not change.
Loops requiring reviewThe server's priority order and up to six rows. Each row keeps its priority, the tag → Investigation, ✓ Acknowledged where present, the diagnosis, the "Why X is here" ? and the in-band bar with its %. Clicking a row previews the loop, and the top row is chosen by default. "n shelved ↗" opens Loop Events (shelved) and View all → opens Performance (Needs attention).
Chosen loopThe tag as its title and Review → to Investigation. The live PV, SP, OP and MODE pills and Signal quality. The rolling 8 h chart keeps its design: PV, SP and OP pens from --signal-*, the PV band, both axes, the legend, Fit to data | Engineering range, 260 px. The signal-mapping and Pipeline Health links stay when nothing is stored.
Recent eventsThe three newest episodes in the plant scope. A row opens Investigation at the episode's opening window. All events → opens Loop Events, narrowed to a loop you chose.
BehaviourEvery number, denominator and server rule; polling every 60 s; the "No monitored loops" warning with its Loop Registry link; error boxes with Retry.
Not proposed againThe stale notice and "—" on cards where nothing was measured. You left them as they are on 11 Nov, so the cards still read 0.

Every action, still reachable

  • Each KPI drill-down: its card, unchanged.
  • Loops needing attention in Performance: View all → (today also "View all loops" and "All loops in Performance →", which opened the same page).
  • Shelved loops: "n shelved ↗" in the queue head.
  • A loop's Investigation: the row's tag, Review →, or an event row.
  • A loop's live signals and trend: click a row, or open ?loop=. To zoom, or to see source and feed times, name and section: Trend, Historical and Loop Explorer.
  • All events: All events →.
  • Pipeline Health and signal mapping: the chosen loop's empty-trend line, as today.
  • Loop Registry: the sidebar (the page-foot link goes).
  • The calculation rules and the trend's band note: How to read (question 1). Each card's rule on hover and each drill-down's ? stay.

For you to decide

  1. Where does Calculation basis go? (a) How to read, top right beside 12h / 24h, in three parts: "The cards" (today's sentence as four rows), "Loops requiring review" (the order rule, so the queue's head loses its ?) and "The trend" (the shaded-band note, so the chart loses its ? on the Overview). (b) Nowhere new: every card's hover already states its own rule, including "newest 12h result ≤ 60 min old", and every drill-down's ? has the rule, formula and threshold, so the sentence just goes. Recommended: (a), because every other redesigned page has How to read in that place, and a touch screen has no hover. No backend change.
  2. Remove the Top-priority finding? It is the queue's first row a second time, and with rows that loop is also the one the chosen-loop panel shows. When empty, it repeats the queue's "nothing to show". Recommended: remove it. No backend change.
  3. Recent events: only the page's window? Every lab episode exists as a 12h and a 24h copy, so today the 12h page shows PIC40102 twice. (a) Client only: read the 12 newest episodes and show the first three of the page's window. (b) A window filter on GET events/page, which is exact but a small cplm-api change. (c) Leave it as it is. Recommended: (a), with no backend change. All events → keeps opening both kinds.
  4. The shorter empty-trend line: everywhere? The trend is shared with Loop Explorer and Investigation, which show the same "no signal values in this trend range" block. (a) The one line, "No PV, SP or OP values in the last 8 h" (or "in this range"), everywhere. (b) On the Overview only. Recommended: (a), so the three pages say it the same way. No backend change.
  5. When nothing live arrives, show only Signal quality? Today four "—" pills sit beside "Signal quality · No signal" (badge 12). Recommended: yes, show only Signal quality, with the four pills back as soon as a value arrives. Overview only, no backend change.

With the recommended answers, nothing changes in a backend or service: it is ams-frontend only.
